chief_complaint: Follow-up for coronary artery disease, hypertension, and metabolic syndrome with ongoing cardiovascular risk management.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of an acute NSTEMI in 2017 and subsequent coronary artery disease. Since then he has been maintained on secondary prevention therapy including aspirin, prasugrel, a high‑intensity statin, beta‑blocker, ACE‑inhibitor, calcium‑channel blocker, and thiazide diuretic. Essential hypertension diagnosed in 2013 is treated with four agents and is currently well controlled (116/72 mmHg). He meets criteria for metabolic syndrome (obesity, pre‑diabetes with A1c 6.4%, dyslipidemia) and reports chronic stress, unhealthy alcohol use, and intimate‑partner abuse, all contributing to his risk profile. Chronic pain and sinusitis are present but not actively treated. Recent laboratory data (lipids, eGFR, BMI) are missing, limiting full risk assessment. The patient works full‑time and has a history of higher education. No acute complaints are documented in the recent visits.

active_problems.name: Acute non‑ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include primary dental caries (2024), gingivitis (2022), acute viral pharyngitis (2022), limited social contact (2020‑2023), prior part‑time employment, and earlier episodes of stress that have resolved. No chronic diseases beyond those listed as active have been documented as resolved.

active_medications.purpose: Antiplatelet therapy post‑PCI for NSTEMI (P2Y12 inhibitor)

active_medications.name: atenolol
active_medications.purpose: Beta‑blocker for coronary artery disease and hypertension

social_determinants: Full‑time employment; ongoing stress; unhealthy alcohol consumption; history of intimate partner abuse; higher education; involvement in risk activities. These factors may affect medication adherence, cardiovascular risk, and mental health.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular: High risk for recurrent ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and peripheral arterial disease due to prior NSTEMI, hypertension, metabolic syndrome, obesity, pre‑diabetes, dyslipidemia, smoking not documented but alcohol use present, and age >55. Renal: Elevated risk for chronic kidney disease from long‑standing hypertension and possible nephrotoxic exposures; eGFR unavailable. Metabolic: High risk for progression to type 2 diabetes given pre‑diabetes, obesity, and metabolic syndrome. Hematologic: Chronic anemia may worsen myocardial oxygen delivery and could indicate CKD or iron deficiency; no anemia‑specific therapy recorded. Neurologic: Vascular risk factors (hypertension, dyslipidemia, alcohol) increase risk for stroke and vascular cognitive impairment.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing; obesity documented but no quantitative BMI.
Renal function (eGFR) not available; cannot stage CKD.
Lipid panel results missing; statin dose may be sub‑optimal.
Medication list lacks explicit indication mapping for several drugs (e.g., aspirin, prasugrel, atenolol).
No iron, B12, or erythropoietin therapy documented despite chronic anemia.
No antidiabetic medication (e.g., metformin) or documented lifestyle intervention.
No analgesic or neuropathic pain medication recorded.

clinical_impression: The patient is a middle‑aged male with high cardiovascular risk driven by prior NSTEMI, resistant hypertension, and metabolic syndrome. Blood pressure is well controlled, but lipid management appears sub‑optimal and renal function data are lacking. Psychosocial stressors, alcohol use, and a history of intimate partner abuse further compound risk and may affect adherence. Overall clinical picture is one of complex, high‑risk secondary prevention requiring comprehensive risk factor optimization and closer monitoring of renal and metabolic parameters.
